title: Secure class-unit checkpoint publication
objective: Publish class-unit checkpoints through unpredictable exclusively created same-directory files, preserve the descriptor through write and fsync, atomically replace, and sync the parent directory where supported

handoff.summary: Replaced predictable pathname-reopened checkpoint temporaries with 128-bit random same-directory candidates created atomically and exclusively at mode 0600. Sage.js now exposes minimal descriptor open/write/fsync/close support through the Node host: exclusive creation maps to `wx`, writes and fsync operate on the original descriptor, short writes are retried, the descriptor closes before atomic replace, and the parent directory is fsynced on supported non-Windows hosts. Collision, pre-created symlink, post-open unlink/symlink replacement, restrictive-mode, cleanup, partial-write, and durability-order regressions cover both the generic os boundary and the class-unit publisher.
risks: The parent-directory fsync is intentionally skipped on Windows and tolerates platform errors that explicitly report the operation unsupported; file-descriptor fsync remains mandatory.
The descriptor API supports the two combinations needed here (read-only and exclusive writable creation), not the complete CPython os.open flag matrix.
Atomic publication does not arbitrate multiple legitimate writers targeting the same final checkpoint; the last atomic replacement wins.

The arithmetic-algebra lane claims were narrowly expanded to shared host/os files with explicit coordinator authorization because genuine same-descriptor safety cannot be implemented in the checkpoint module alone.

The lane checker still reports the authorized src/lib/os.py and tools/host.ts claims as outside its static arithmetic-algebra allowlist; integration must review those two shared-file changes explicitly.
Broad native and merged-suite gates were deferred; focused Sage.js host/context runtime regressions, ordinary CPython parsing, and direct zero-error Pyright are recorded.
next_steps: Run the full stdlib and class-unit suites on merged main, including native Windows CI for the `wx`/fsync/replace path.
Consider expanding os.open only when another audited caller needs additional flag combinations; do not silently accept unsupported semantics.
Retain the descriptor-preserving host operations if the built-in file object is later refactored, because reopening a temp pathname after exclusive creation reintroduces the race.
